tables.title: Hex cap screws
tables.reference: ASME B18.2.1-2012 Table 6, pp. 10-11; fillets Table 10, p. 17
notes: Threads per inch are the ASME B1.1 coarse (UNC) and fine (UNF) series (Machinery's Handbook 26th Table 2, p. 1715); the dimension table itself does not list them. Sizes with no coarse thread (1 5/8, 1 7/8, over 4 in) and the fine series over 1 1/2 in (12-UN) are blank.
Thread series may be UNC, UNF or 8-UN (B18.2.1 para. 2.5.3); steel bolts and screws are usually to SAE J429 or ASTM A307/A449/A354 (grade and material, not dimensions).
F and H basic are the printed fractions as decimals.
J is the wrenching height: from the bearing surface up the corners, over which G must be held.
R is the long-screw underhead fillet of Table 10, which has no 1 5/8 or 1 7/8 row.
LT for L over 6 in is not given for 2 1/4 in and larger (all those are 6 in and longer).
Y (reference) is five coarse threads; FIM is the maximum runout of the bearing surface.
The "finished hex bolt" of earlier editions is today's hex cap screw (Foreword, p. v).

tables.title: Heavy hex structural bolts
tables.reference: ASME B18.2.6-1996 Table 1, p. 6
notes: Read from a scan of the 1996 edition. The bolts of ASTM F3125 (A325, A490, F1852, F2280) are made to these dimensions, with UNC-2A threads (the fine series is not used).
LT is the thread length for all bolt lengths (reference); bolts are shorter-threaded than B18.2.1 heavy hex bolts so that the threads stay out of the shear plane.
F and H basic are the printed fractions as decimals.

tables.title: Socket head cap screws
tables.reference: ASME B18.3-1998 Table 4 as in Machinery's Handbook 26th p. 1601; LT from the Unbrako Engineering Guide (2004) p. 6
notes: Threads per inch are the ASME B1.1 coarse (UNC) and fine (UNF) series (Machinery's Handbook 26th Table 2, p. 1715); the dimension table itself does not list them. Sizes with no coarse thread (1 5/8, 1 7/8, over 4 in) and the fine series over 1 1/2 in (12-UN) are blank.
1960 series. Threads are Class 3A UNRC/UNRF to 1 in, 2A to 1 1/2 in, 2A UNRC above.
Alloy steel screws are to ASTM A574 (and stainless to ASTM F837): these set material, not dimensions.
J is the hex key size (nominal); M the spline socket size, not made over 1 in.
F is the fillet's extension above D (the fillet is given as an extension, not a radius).
LT is Unbrako's thread length (manufacturer's data, to 3 in; B18.3 as Machinery's reproduces it gives none). The 9/16 size Unbrako lists is not in B18.3-1998 and is left out.
Machinery's reproduces the 1998 edition; no copy of B18.3 itself is in the library. Unbrako's dimensions agree with it wherever both give one.

tables.title: Button head socket cap screws
tables.reference: ASME B18.3-1998 Table 7 as in Machinery's Handbook 26th p. 1604; T from the Unbrako Engineering Guide (2004) p. 15
notes: Threads per inch are the ASME B1.1 coarse (UNC) and fine (UNF) series (Machinery's Handbook 26th Table 2, p. 1715); the dimension table itself does not list them. Sizes with no coarse thread (1 5/8, 1 7/8, over 4 in) and the fine series over 1 1/2 in (12-UN) are blank.
For light fastening (guards, covers); not for critical high-strength joints.
Material: ASTM F835 (alloy steel) or F879 (stainless); the dimensions are B18.3's.
T is Unbrako's minimum key engagement (manufacturer's data): Machinery's does not reproduce it.
J is the hex key size (nominal).

tables.title: Flat countersunk head socket cap screws
tables.reference: ASME B18.3-1998 Table 6 as in Machinery's Handbook 26th p. 1603; gage diameter and protrusion from the Unbrako Engineering Guide (2004) p. 14
notes: Threads per inch are the ASME B1.1 coarse (UNC) and fine (UNF) series (Machinery's Handbook 26th Table 2, p. 1715); the dimension table itself does not list them. Sizes with no coarse thread (1 5/8, 1 7/8, over 4 in) and the fine series over 1 1/2 in (12-UN) are blank.
Head angle 82° +0/-2°. A max is to the theoretical sharp corners, A min the absolute minimum with the edge flat.
Material: ASTM F835 (alloy steel) or F879 (stainless); the dimensions are B18.3's.
G and P are Unbrako's gage diameter and the head's protrusion above it (manufacturer's data, to 1 in): Machinery's does not reproduce them.
The 1 1/2 in row is garbled in Machinery's text layer ("10 . 4 3 5"); read as J 1, T 0.435.
Unbrako prints A min 1.855 for 1 in where B18.3-1998 gives 1.841 (0.95 A max, as the larger sizes); the standard's value is kept.

tables.title: Low head socket cap screws
tables.reference: Unbrako Socket Products Engineering Guide (2004) p. 11
notes: Manufacturer's data: ASME B18.3 has no inch low head cap screw (the metric one is DIN 7984 / B18.3.1M's low head type). Other makers' low heads differ.
Material ASTM A574 alloy steel (Unbrako). Threads Class 3A UNRC/UNRF.
Threads run to within two threads of the head on stock lengths.

tables.title: Hex nuts
tables.reference: ASME B18.2.2-2010 Table 4, p. 8
notes: Threads per inch are the ASME B1.1 coarse (UNC) and fine (UNF) series (Machinery's Handbook 26th Table 2, p. 1715); the dimension table itself does not list them. Sizes with no coarse thread (1 5/8, 1 7/8, over 4 in) and the fine series over 1 1/2 in (12-UN) are blank.
F of 1 5/8 in is printed to two places (2.35, 2.43) where the hex screws print 2.356 and 2.438; G is consistent with the printed F. Values as printed.
Steel nuts are to SAE J995 or ASTM A563 (grade and material, not dimensions).

tables.title: Hex head bolts and screws
tables.reference: Lindstrom Metric technical manual (2008), Section 2 pp. 1-3 (PDF pp. 17-19), ISO 4014/4017 (1988) rows; e min from the Bumax catalogue p. 14; dw, c, ds from Machinery's Handbook 26th ed. Table 1 (ASME B18.2.3.1M), p. 1521
notes: ISO 4014 has a partly threaded shank (thread length b); ISO 4017 is threaded to the head. Head dimensions are the same.
Sizes in brackets in the source (M14, M18, M22, M27, M33, M39, M45, M52, M60) are not preferred for new designs.

DIN 931/933 differ from ISO 4014/4017 in the width across flats of M10 (17), M12 (19), M14 (22) and M22 (32), and slightly in k for M2-M4 and M24; otherwise they are interchangeable. DIN also has M7 (s 11, k 4.8) and M72 (s 105, k 45).
b is a reference length for each range of nominal length l, printed only where ISO 4014 has lengths in that range (blank otherwise); ISO 4017 screws are threaded full length.
k nominal is the middle of the printed limits (ISO tolerances k to js), and agrees with the Bumax catalogue's k where it prints one.

e min: Bumax pp. 12 and 14 (product grade A to M24, B above); where Bumax has no value it is the ISO 4032 nut's e min for the same s and grade (M2, M3, M33-M64); none is given for M22. Bumax p. 12 prints 23.35 for M14, p. 14 23.36; 23.36 is used.

dw min, c and ds are the ASME B18.2.3.1M values (Machinery's Table 1), which match ISO 4014 closely but are not the ISO table; they are blank for sizes B18.2.3.1M lacks. r min (underhead fillet) is not in any source to hand and is left out.

tables.title: Heavy hex structural bolts
tables.reference: Machinery's Handbook 26th ed., Table 11 (ANSI Metric Heavy Hex Structural Bolts), p. 1529
notes: Neither EN 14399-4 (HV) nor ISO 7412 is in the library; this is the ASME metric heavy hex structural bolt (ASTM A325M / A490M) as tabulated in Machinery's Handbook. EN 14399-4 HV bolts differ: s is 32 for M20 (34 here).
B is a basic (reference) thread length; X includes the incomplete threads and tolerances on grip gaging and is for calculation.
Machinery's Table 10 (ASME B18.2.3.6M heavy hex bolts) has the same heads, and also M12 and M14 (S 21 and 24).

tables.title: Socket head cap screws
tables.reference: Lindstrom Metric technical manual (2008), Section 1 pp. 1-2 (PDF pp. 4-5), ISO 4762 (1997) rows; ds and da from Machinery's Handbook 26th ed. Table 23 (ASME B18.3.1M), p. 1539
notes: Head diameter max allows for a knurled head (Lindstrom p. 1); a plain head's dk max is the nominal (ISO 4762: equal to k max for d ≥ M3).
M14 is not preferred for new designs. DIN 912 also has M1.4, M2.6, M18, M22, M27, M33, M39, M45 and M72-M100, which ISO 4762 no longer includes; its other values are the same as ISO's.

ds and da are the ASME B18.3.1M values (Machinery's Table 23), which equal ISO 4762's (ds min is d less the h13 tolerance); B18.3.1M stops at M48, so they are blank for M56 and M64. The underhead fillet r is not in any source to hand.
b is a reference thread length (2d + 12); screws too short for it are threaded close to the head.

tables.title: Button head socket cap screws
tables.reference: Lindstrom Metric technical manual (2008), Section 1 p. 7 (PDF p. 10), ~ISO 7380 (1983) rows
notes: Lindstrom marks its table "~ISO 7380" (approximately ISO 7380:1983) and prints the same socket limits as ASME B18.3.4M; ISO 7380-2:2011 gives s max 2.080, 2.580, 3.080, 4.095, 5.140, 6.140, 8.175, 10.175 for M3-M16, which ISO 7380-1 shares.
Lengths up to a stepped line are threaded to the head; longer ones have a thread length between 2d + 12 and within 2P of the head, at the maker's discretion (Lindstrom p. 7).
Not intended for high-strength applications: 10.9 and 12.9 are made for the socket's wear resistance.

tables.title: Button head socket cap screws with collar
tables.reference: ISO 7380-2:2011 Table 1, p. 1 of the library copy (ISO 7380-2 BHCS.pdf, a scan)
notes: The library copy is the first two pages of the standard: Table 1 is cut off after s, so the key engagement t (and the collar w, v rows if any) are missing.
e min applies to the socket (e = 1.14 s min, ISO 7380-2 footnote).

columns.name: Diameter of the socket's head relief

tables.title: Countersunk (flat) head socket cap screws
tables.reference: Lindstrom Metric technical manual (2008), Section 1 p. 8 (PDF p. 11), ISO 10642 (1997) rows
notes: dk max is theoretical: the diameter of a hole countersunk to exactly 90° in which the largest head sits flush. k is a reference value only.
The nominal length l includes the head. ISO 10642 sets the thread length by a grip-length formula (not tabulated here); DIN 7991 gives b = 2d + 6 (l ≤ 125).

M14 is not preferred. DIN 7991 differs: dk max = nominal 6, 8, 10, 12, 16, 20, 24, 27, 30, 36 and k max 1.7, 2.3, 2.8, 3.3, 4.4, 5.5, 6.5, 7, 7.5, 8.5 for M3-M20, and also has M2, M2.5, M18, M22 and M24.
Not intended for high-strength applications: 10.9 and 12.9 are made for the socket's wear resistance.

tables.title: Low head socket cap screws
tables.reference: DIN 7984:1985-05 (SMS reprint 1998), Seite 2-3, read from the scan (Din-7984.pdf)
notes: Product grade A. Sizes in brackets in the standard (M14, M18, M22) are to be avoided.
b is an auxiliary (reference) value ("Hilfsmaß"), printed only for the length ranges the size comes in.
e min = 1.14 × s min (the socket's corners). f max = 1.7 r max, r max = (da max - ds max) / 2.

The low head and the small socket put the critical section under the socket, not in the thread: the standard recommends these screws not be used to carry high preload (about 70 % of the 8.8 yield is what a DIN 911 key can apply).
The values agree with Lindstrom Metric's manual (2008), Section 1 p. 5.

tables.title: Hex nuts, style 1
tables.reference: Lindstrom Metric technical manual (2008), Section 3 pp. 1-3 (PDF pp. 25-27), ISO 4032 (1986) rows
notes: Fine-pitch nuts of the same dimensions are ISO 8673; the extra-fine pitches the source also lists are M10 × 1, M12 × 1.25 and M18-M24 × 1.5.
Sizes in brackets in the source (M3.5, M18, M22, M27, M33, M39, M45, M52, M60) and fine pitches are not preferred for new designs.

DIN 934 differs from ISO 4032 in s for M10 (17), M12 (19), M14 (22) and M22 (32), and in thickness: DIN 934's m is about 0.8 d (M5 4.0, M6 5.0, M8 6.5, M10 8.0, M12 10.0, M16 13.0, M20 16.0, M24 19.0, M30 24.0, M36 29.0 max) against ISO's thicker nut (about 0.9 d) for M5-M39.
ISO 4032 e min is the product-grade value: grade A to M16, B above.

tables.title: Heavy hex nuts
tables.reference: Machinery's Handbook 26th ed., Table 31 (Metric Hex Jam Nuts and Heavy Hex Nuts), p. 1548
notes: The nut for the heavy hex structural bolts (iso.heavyHexBolt). Neither EN 14399-4 (HV nuts) nor ISO 4775 is in the library: this is the ASME metric heavy hex nut as tabulated in Machinery's Handbook.
Machinery's (p. 1542) says B18.2.4.6M was coordinated with draft ISO standards in sizes M12 to M36, with differences that do not affect interchangeability; M42-M100 are as the table prints them.

tables.title: Thin hex nuts (jam nuts)
tables.reference: Lindstrom Metric technical manual (2008), Section 3 pp. 4-5 (PDF pp. 28-29), ISO 4035 (1986) / ISO 8675 (1988) rows
notes: ISO 4035 is the coarse-pitch thin nut; ISO 8675 the fine-pitch one, with the same dimensions.
DIN 439 B has the same thicknesses; its s differs for M10 (17), M12 (19), M14 (22) and M22 (32).
Sizes in brackets in the source (M3.5, M18, M22, M27, M33, M39, M45, M52) and fine pitches are not preferred for new designs. The source has no M60.

tables.reference: ASME B18.2.6-1996 Table 3, p. 11 (1/2 to 1 1/2 in); Portland Bolt, F436 hardened washers (dimensions per ASTM F436; 1 5/8 to 4 in)
notes: Through-hardened steel washers for high-strength structural bolts (ASTM F3125 / A325, A490): the washers AISC 360 and the RCSC specification call for. Type 1 carbon steel, Type 3 weathering steel; hardness 38-45 HRC, 26-45 HRC galvanized (Portland Bolt).

Portland Bolt prints the 1 and 1 1/8 in inside diameters as 1 1/16 and 1 3/16 in; B18.2.6 gives 1.125 and 1.250 (used here). Its other 1/2 to 1 1/2 in values agree with B18.2.6.

Over 1 1/2 in only nominal sizes and thickness limits are given (Portland Bolt); B18.2.6-1996 stops at 1 1/2 in, and ASTM F436 itself is not in the library. Extra thick (5/16 in) F436 washers are not listed.

notes: Normal (standard) series. Values from Lindstrom's DIN 125 / ISO 7089 table, not from either standard (neither is in the library); the Bumax catalogue agrees at M6-M12. ISO 7090 / DIN 125-B are the same washers chamfered.
